headline: Face coverings retained after a University Management Committee review
detail: Reviewed on 22 October and kept, with a further review set for 6 December.
quote: Following a University Management Committee (UMC) review on 22 October, UCL will retain its existing guidance on face coverings. This will be reviewed again on 6 December.
notes: Filed on 22 October, the date of the review; reported 25 October. The second documented decision to stay stricter than the law required.

headline: Traffic light travel system replaced by a Red List of seven countries
detail: UCL permitted business travel to any country not on the Red List where the need was justified.
quote: The UK Government has replaced the “traffic light” system for international travel with a single Red List of seven countries where travel is not allowed.
notes: The loosest travel position since March 2020. It lasted five weeks before Omicron.

headline: Face coverings made mandatory indoors on campus as Omicron emerges
detail: Following the Prime Minister's announcement of precautionary measures on 27 November.
quote: Face coverings are mandatory for all students and staff while you are indoors on campus, unless you are exempt.
notes: A move from expected to mandatory. UCL's own advisory panel is named alongside government guidance as the basis.

headline: All UCL-sponsored staff social gatherings cancelled
detail: Applying to any gathering where UCL contributed to costs, on or off campus, with teams strongly advised to postpone parties.
quote: In response to the uncertainty arising from the Omicron variant, we have agreed that all UCL-sponsored social gatherings should be cancelled or postponed until further notice.
notes: Explicitly to protect teaching: cutting non-essential gatherings so that essential activity could continue. Lifted on 7 February 2022.

headline: Staff encouraged to work remotely to December to cut campus footfall
detail: With campus staying open for in-person teaching, research and support.
quote: However, to minimise footfall and ensure our spaces are as safe as possible for those staff who do need to work on campus, we encourage you to speak to your manager about whether more of your work could be carried out remotely until the end of December.
notes: Two months after all staff were told to return. This is the reversal that precedes the highest weekly case count in the whole series.

headline: Plan B: office workers to work from home, with higher education exempted
detail: Face coverings required by law in most indoor public places from 10 December, NHS COVID Pass for large venues from 15 December, though not for teaching events.
quote: From Monday 13 December, office workers should work from home if they can, with Government exemptions for Higher Education staff (see below).
notes: Filed on 13 December, the effective date; announced by the government on 8 December and by UCL on 9 December, a one-day lag. The higher education exemption is why UCL stayed open and why the December case counts are as high as they are.

headline: UCL states cases are rising on campus as well as nationally
quote: Just as numbers of COVID-19 cases are rising throughout the UK, including the new Omicron variant, so too are they on campus.
notes: The clearest instance in the whole record of UCL acting on its own case data rather than on national policy: the newsletter cites the campus figures directly, and the on-campus student series peaks at its highest point of the entire dataset in the week to 21 December. This is the passage quoted in the blog post.

headline: Staff permitted to move teaching online for the final week of Term 1
detail: At the discretion of the programme and Head of Department, with no requirement to do so.
quote: Whilst campus remains open for face-to-face teaching and other activities until term ends on Friday, you may move your teaching online for the remainder of this week.
notes: Permission rather than instruction, and taken eight days before the on-campus student peak of 525 cases in the week to 21 December 2021. Whether the permission was widely used cannot be established from the archive.

headline: Winter closure extended by a day to 23 December
quote: UCL's winter closure has been extended by one day to include Thursday, 23 December 2021 in recognition of our community's hard work over a difficult year

headline: Term 2 to open with face-to-face teaching, disruption anticipated
detail: Campus open, large teaching events online, all students including those overseas told to come to campus.
quote: Our plan for Term 2 is for campus to remain open and for face-to-face teaching to go ahead as it has this term, which means of course that large teaching events will continue online and all students, including students based overseas, have been told that they should come to campus.
notes: Decided at the peak of the Omicron wave, with UCL's own case counts at their highest. Campus stayed open because government and UCL's public health experts both advised it.

headline: UCL expects two to three weeks of disruption at the start of January
detail: From delayed student arrivals and from staff and student absence through self-isolation.
quote: we should anticipate that the first 2-3 weeks in January will be disrupted, including some students facing delays in getting back to London. We can also expect an increase in absences among students required to self-isolate
notes: A forecast made in December that the January 2022 data can be read against. January 2022 is the month the blog post compares with January 2021.

headline: Staff who are unvaccinated by choice must still attend campus
detail: Staff unable to be vaccinated for medical reasons were not required to attend and teaching staff in that group could work remotely.
quote: Colleagues who are unable to be vaccinated for medical reasons are not required to attend campus, and teaching staff in this category may deliver learning remotely. Staff who are unvaccinated through choice must attend campus as per the normal requirements of their duties.
notes: The only place in the record where vaccination status carries a direct consequence for a member of staff's attendance, and it distinguishes medical exemption from choice.

headline: COVID absence paid and exempt from the sickness procedure for up to four weeks
detail: With no medical evidence required for the first 28 days of absences beginning between 10 December 2021 and 26 January 2022.
quote: Any COVID-19 related absence from work will be paid and will not trigger the usual Sickness Absence Procedure unless it lasts more than four weeks or 20 working days in total (pro-rata for part-time staff).
notes: A limit put on the open-ended commitment of 17 March 2020, which had exempted COVID absence from the procedure entirely.

headline: Plan B removed and UCL reinstates the 40% on-campus expectation
detail: Work-from-home guidance, vaccine certificates and the legal mask requirement all lifted nationally.
quote: From Thursday 27 January, we will reinstate UCL’s Interim People Management Guidance , including the expectation for all staff to work on campus for at least 40% of the time.
notes: Filed on 27 January, the effective date; announced 20 January. Restores the settlement agreed in May 2021 after the Omicron interruption.

headline: Face coverings kept mandatory at UCL after the legal requirement ended
quote: As part of our measures to reduce the risk of infection, face coverings will remain mandatory at UCL while you are indoors in our buildings, unless you are exempt.
notes: The third and last documented divergence in the cautious direction, and the longest-running: UCL held a mask requirement from 10 July 2020 to 21 February 2022.

headline: Restriction on staff social gatherings lifted and event size limits removed
detail: With risk assessments still encouraged and the face coverings policy still in force.
quote: The restriction on holding UCL-sponsored staff gatherings, introduced in December 2021 in response to the emergence of the Omicron variant of coronavirus, has now been lifted.
notes: Ten weeks after the December cancellation.

headline: UCL's asymptomatic testing centre closes
detail: Replaced by a home test kit collection service on the Student Centre mezzanine.
quote: UCL’s asymptomatic testing centre in the Student Centre will close this Friday, 18 February. From Monday 21 February staff and students will be able to collect LFTs from the Home Test Kit Collection Service on the mezzanine level of the Student Centre
notes: The end of UCL's own testing provision, fifteen months after it opened at Bidborough House. Case ascertainment falls from here on, so the declining case counts in spring 2022 partly reflect less testing.

headline: Face coverings narrowed to teaching settings only
detail: Strongly advised elsewhere in crowded and enclosed spaces, following discussion by the University Management Committee, the Workplace Health and Safety Committee and the Public Health Advisory Panel.
quote: From Monday 21 February, we expect students and staff to continue wearing face coverings in teaching settings and strongly advise you to continue to wear a face covering in crowded and enclosed spaces in other settings where you may come into contact with people you do not normally meet (unless you are exempt).
notes: The first relaxation of the face covering policy since it was introduced, and it comes three and a half weeks after Plan B ended rather than with it.

headline: Remaining domestic restrictions removed and UCL adopts living safely guidance
detail: The final newsletter of the series, relaying the government's advice on living safely with respiratory infections including COVID-19.
quote: The Government has removed remaining domestic COVID-19 restrictions in England and has published advice on living safely with respiratory infections including COVID-19 , which includes measures such as getting vaccinated, keeping spaces well-ventilated and practicing good hygiene.
notes: Issue 165, the last of the 168 files. It is not on UCL's index page and was fetched separately; manifest.csv records this.

headline: Twice-weekly testing advice dropped as free national testing ends
quote: In line with Government guidance and the end of the free national testing programme, we no longer advise staff and students to test for COVID-19 twice a week.
notes: The end of routine testing, and therefore of the mechanism that generated the case data. The published series stops a week later, on 11 May 2022, which is the reason the record ends: the counting stopped, not the pandemic.

headline: Connect to Protect kept running for reporting positive cases
quote: Please continue to use UCL’s Connect to Protect service to report positive cases, so that we can monitor cases and identify potential outbreaks.
notes: Reporting was retained after testing advice was withdrawn, so the collection mechanism outlived the thing that fed it. Whether the public page continued to be updated is answered by the data, not the newsletters: the last row of covid_raw.csv is 2022-05-11.

headline: Face coverings no longer expected anywhere on campus
detail: Except in areas managed by partner hospitals, with individual choice acknowledged.
quote: In line with Government guidance, staff, students and visitors are no longer expected to wear face coverings or masks on campus.
notes: The end of a requirement that ran, in one form or another, from 22 May 2020.

headline: Unlimited COVID carers leave reverts to five days a year
quote: Parents and carers leave for COVID-19 related absences will no longer be unlimited and will revert to 5 days per year from 1 May
notes: Closes the commitment made on 19 March 2020 that caring responsibilities would not cost staff leave or pay. Filed on 1 May, the effective date; reported 4 May.

headline: COVID-19 telephone helpline closed
quote: The COVID-19 telephone helpline service has now ended.
notes: The helpline had run since June 2020. Its closure in the final newsletter is the clearest marker that UCL considered the emergency over.
